dana: Quick q — for onboarding canaries, do we want dataset-driven evals to run in the same pod as the smokebench or as a separate scheduled job? Thinking about cost and isolation.
kevin: separate job + ephemeral pods. Cheaper to scale independently. also easier to snapshot datasets. :thumbsup:
olivia: separate job makes sense. but what about KV cache warming? if it's separate we lose warm cache and can mis-estimate latency.
sahil: can add a lightweight warmup step that replays prefixes into the same node before measuring. 10-30s per model should be enough.
taylor: or run warmups on a small pool that mirrors prod nodes. cost increase but better fidelity.
dana: tradeoff table please: fidelity vs cost vs complexity. can someone sketch numbers?
kevin: rough numbers: warmup pool = +20% cost per canary, latency fidelity + ~10-15%. separate job (no warmup) = base cost, fidelity - ~25% on p99.
olivia: also consider batching. our smokebench continuous batcher hides latency tail. For canary we should measure both single-request latency and queued throughput.
sahil: agree. propose two-phase canary: phase1 single-request cold-run (no batching), phase2 throughput run with batching enabled.
dana: nice. how do we orchestrate datasets? small golden set + stratified sample from live traffic?
kevin: golden set for regressions. stratified sampled historical requests for perf/throughput. store snapshots in s3 with version tag. example schedule:
```
canary:
  on_push: true
  nightly: "02:00 UTC"
  regions: ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"]
```
taylor: scheduling: run canaries on model push + nightly for drift detection. Stagger across regions to smooth cost.
dana: what's the runbook for failures? if canary fails perf but passes quality, auto-block rollout?
olivia: default: perf regressions that exceed threshold should block. quality regressions always block. ops can override with reason.
sahil: add an automatic rollback policy in deployment config and a slack alert that pings #eng-oncall and the model owner.
dana: sample alert text?
kevin: "deploy-bot: Canary for model foo@v3 failed perf: p99 latency +40% vs baseline. Rollout paused. /cc @olivia @dana"
deploy-bot: Canary job 1739998895 completed: status=FAIL, perf_regressions=1, quality_regressions=0. logs: https://ci.internal/canaries/1739998895
taylor: nice. last q: how long do canaries run? 10-15 minutes enough for stable traffic?
olivia: for latency you can do 10m with synthetic load. for throughput maybe 30-60m depending on burstiness.
dana: assigning action items: @kevin sketch cost/fidelity numbers, @sahil prototype warmup step, @taylor draft scheduling cadence + infra change. Back here EOD? :eyes:
kevin: on it.
sahil: I'll start a PR with warmup hook.
taylor: will post a calendar with proposed cadence.
